package.name: elevenlabs
package.packageFile:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/package.schema.json

# ELEVENLABS, fully declarative — all five nodes.
#
# ALL FIVE, not four, and that is forced rather than ambitious: they share ONE credential, and
# declaration is all-or-nothing per package (`registerCredentialType` is first-wins and silent, so a
# credentials/*.yaml alongside a live registerCredential() means one of them vanishes at random). So
# SpeechToText could not be left behind — which is why `encoding: multipart` was built first.
#
# FOUR SHAPES, ONE PACKAGE:
#   TTS, Dialogue, Music, SoundEffects   POST JSON, receive raw audio bytes → transport: binary
#   SpeechToText                         POST a FORM carrying the audio file → encoding: multipart
#
# ONE PATH DROPPED, deliberately, and it is worth reading before assuming it was an oversight. The TTS
# node also carried a MULTI-SPEAKER COMPAT path: it sniffed [DETECTIVE]: labels out of the text, mapped
# them to hardcoded voice pools, tried /text-to-dialogue, and on failure fell back to one TTS call per
# segment with the mp3 buffers CONCATENATED. That concatenation is byte work no manifest can describe.
#
# It is gone because its reason is gone. The path existed to preserve the MurderMystery app, which is now
# in _legacy/; `characterId` and `characterGender` appear nowhere in apps/ outside the node's own files;
# and the service's own header already said "for general multi-speaker work prefer the dedicated
# ElevenLabs Dialogue node", which is in this package and takes explicit per-line voices. So the
# capability is not lost, it moved to the node built for it.

name: elevenlabs
displayName: ElevenLabs
description: Speech, dialogue, music and sound effects from ElevenLabs
version: 2.0.0
category: media
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1768540562/gravity/icons/elevanlabs.jpg

features:
  - Text to speech, dialogue, music and sound effects
  - Transcription with word-level timings

allowedHosts:
  - api.elevenlabs.io

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  # `binary` for the four generators, `json` for transcription's reply.
  transport: [binary, json]
  encoding: [multipart]

credentials.elevenlabsCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

# The TYPE NAME is kept exactly as it was when these nodes lived in `ingest`, so credentials already
# stored against it keep resolving. A credential is selected by type name, so renaming it would leave
# every existing workflow authenticating with nothing.
name: elevenlabsCredential
displayName: ElevenLabs
description: ElevenLabs API credentials for text-to-speech, sound effects, and transcription

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your ElevenLabs API key from the dashboard (Profile then API Keys)
    placeholder: Enter your ElevenLabs API key

shared.audio.yaml:
# THE AUDIO OUTPUT, shared by the four generators.
#
# `response` is the BINARY reply handed over as { base64, contentType } — what `transport: binary`
# produces, and the same shape a `multipart` file part consumes, so bytes have ONE representation
# everywhere they travel in this platform.
#
# Shared because four nodes emit the identical object and a fifth will: the day the shape changes, it
# changes once.

out: >-
  return { data: response.base64, mimeType: response.contentType || 'audio/mpeg', fileName: 'audio.mp3' }
shared.credential.yaml:
# ElevenLabs authenticates with `xi-api-key`, on every call in the package.
#
# Shared because repeating it five times is five chances to mistype the header name, and a wrong header
# is a 401 that reads like a bad key rather than a bad manifest.

scheme: apiKeyHeader
header: xi-api-key
value: "{{ credentials.elevenlabsCredential.apiKey }}"

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: text
  value: "return response.text || ''"

- emit: metadata
  # `words` carries the per-word timings, which is the whole reason to use this over a plain transcript —
  # a caption track or a seek-to-word UI is built from it. Defaulted to [] so a consumer can always map.
  value: >-
    return {
      languageCode: response.language_code,
      languageProbability: response.language_probability,
      words: Array.isArray(response.words) ? response.words : []
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# THE ONE MULTIPART CALL in the package, and the reason `encoding: multipart` was built: this endpoint
# takes the audio as a FORM PART, which no JSON body can express.
#
# TWO WAYS TO SUPPLY AUDIO, and the form field differs for each — transcribed from the service:
#   base64  a FILE part. `{ base64, mimeType, filename }` is the shape the executor turns back into
#           bytes, the same shape `transport: binary` produces, so audio from another node flows straight in
#   a URL   a plain TEXT field, `source_url`, and the vendor fetches it itself
#
# The URL WINS when both are set, matching the service's if/else. Each field is an expression returning
# undefined when it does not apply, so exactly one of them appears in the form — `resolveBody` drops the
# other, and sending both would be ambiguous.
#
# NO Content-Type IS DECLARED. The boundary is fetch's to generate, and a multipart header without one is
# a body the vendor cannot split.

- name: transcribe
  method: POST
  url: https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/speech-to-text
  credential: { $ref: credential }
  encoding: multipart

  body:
    model_id: "{{ config.modelId }}"
    source_url: "return String(config.audioUrl || '').trim() || undefined"
    file: >-
      return String(config.audioUrl || '').trim() ? undefined
        : (config.audioBase64
            ? { base64: config.audioBase64, mimeType: config.mimeType || 'audio/mpeg', filename: 'audio' }
            : undefined)
    language_code: "{{ config.languageCode }}"
    # Sent only when true, and as the STRING "true": a form carries text, and the service set it that way.
    diarize: "return config.diarize ? 'true' : undefined"
    tag_audio_events: "return config.tagAudioEvents ? 'true' : undefined"

  timeoutMs: 300000
  # JSON back, not audio — the only node here that reads a document rather than bytes.
  transport: json

  # NEITHER SOURCE SET is the one error worth naming ourselves. Without this the vendor answers a 400
  # about a missing file, which does not tell an author that the field they left blank was `audioUrl`.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.detail || !!response.error"
    message: >-
      return (response.detail && (response.detail.message || JSON.stringify(response.detail)))
        || response.error
        || 'Transcription failed. Provide audioUrl or audioBase64.'
files.config.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  # NEITHER source is required by the schema, because exactly ONE of them must be set and a schema cannot
  # say "one of these two". The call's `error` block says it instead, at the only point where both values
  # are known.
  required: []
  properties:
    audioUrl:
      type: string
      title: Audio URL
      description: >-
        A URL ElevenLabs can fetch. Use this OR Audio (base64), not both — the URL wins if both are set.
      default: "{{{input}}}"
      "ui:field": template
    audioBase64:
      type: string
      title: Audio (base64)
      description: >-
        The audio itself, base64 encoded — what an upstream node emits as `audio.data`. Use it when the
        file is not reachable by URL.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    mimeType:
      type: string
      title: MIME Type
      description: Content type of the base64 audio, e.g. audio/mpeg. Ignored when using a URL.
      default: audio/mpeg
    modelId:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: Override the transcription model. Leave blank for the package default.
      default: ""
    languageCode:
      type: string
      title: Language
      description: ISO code, e.g. en. Leave blank to auto-detect.
      default: ""
    diarize:
      type: boolean
      title: Identify Speakers
      description: Label which speaker said each word
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    tagAudioEvents:
      type: boolean
      title: Tag Audio Events
      description: Mark laughter, applause and similar non-speech sounds
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
"ui:order":
  [audioUrl, audioBase64, mimeType, languageCode, diarize, tagAudioEvents, modelId]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: string
    required: false
    description: Audio URL to transcribe, when not set in config

outputs:
  - name: text
    type: string
    description: The full transcript
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: languageCode, languageProbability, words (with timings)

credentials:
  - name: elevenlabsCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/node.schema.json

type: ElevenLabsSpeechToText
kind: PromiseNode

name: ElevenLabs Speech to Text
category: Media & Design
color: "#FF69B4"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1768540562/gravity/icons/elevanlabs.jpg

description: Transcribe audio to text with word-level timings and optional speaker labels.

whenToUse: >-
  Turn RECORDED AUDIO into text: a meeting, a voice note, an interview, a video's soundtrack. It reads
  audio and returns words, which is the opposite direction to every other node in this package. Ask for
  diarization when you need to know who spoke.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Transcription IS deterministic for a given file, but the input is usually a URL whose contents can
  # change, and a wrong cached transcript is worse than a slow one.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/test.schema.json

# Needs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and a REACHABLE audio URL — ElevenLabs fetches it server-side, so a localhost
# path cannot work. The URL below is a placeholder rather than a real file: inventing one that happened to
# resolve would make this fixture pass for a reason nobody chose.
#
# It exercises the URL path. The base64 path is the one that needs multipart's FILE part, and that is
# covered against a real server in packages/base/tests/manifest-multipart.test.ts — including that the
# bytes survive the round trip, which no live fixture could assert without a known file.

testData:
  config:
    audioUrl: https://example.com/sample.mp3
    languageCode: en
    diarize: false
    tagAudioEvents: false
  inputs:
    input: https://example.com/sample.mp3
  expect:
    text: "return typeof output.text === 'string' && output.text.length > 0"
    # `words` must be an ARRAY even when empty, because every consumer maps over it.
    metadata: "return Array.isArray(output.metadata.words)"
